I rebooked every passenger from ZX 440 and ZX 444 except one booking. Booking PD9X3K (4 Economy) is still on ZX 440 because no connection had 4 free Economy seats on every flight.

| Priority | Booking | Passengers | From | New flights | Arrives JFK (9 Nov) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | WN4R8C | 1 Business, 2 Economy | FRA | ZX 470 → ZX 472 (via AMS) | 18:40 |
| 2 | HB3K9W | 1 Business, 1 Economy | MUC | ZX 474 → ZX 472 (via AMS) | 18:40 |
| 3 | LM2Q7H | 2 Business | FRA | ZX 494 → ZX 490 (via BOS) | 20:25 |
| 4 | EK1V7P | 1 Business | MUC | ZX 454 → ZX 462 (via LHR) | 21:55 |
| 5 | PD9X3K | 4 Economy | FRA | Left on ZX 440 | — |
| 6 | OR6M2D | 3 Economy | MUC | ZX 454 → ZX 460 (via LHR) | 17:55 |
| 7 | CB8T4F | 2 Economy | FRA | ZX 494 → ZX 490 (via BOS) | 20:25 |
| 8 | SV5J1N | 1 Economy | FRA | ZX 470 → ZX 472 (via AMS) | 18:40 |

- **Why some groups don't get the earliest flight:** the earliest connections (via LHR on ZX 460, arriving 17:55) had no free Business seats. That pushed the Business groups onto later connections.
- **Ties:** ZX 494 → ZX 490 arrives at 20:25, the same time as a route through DUB and BOS. I picked it because it has one change instead of two.
- **Booking order:** I booked LM2Q7H and CB8T4F together in one step, since both were due on the same flights. The order of bookings doesn't change the result.

ANSWER: PD9X3K

1. Everyone keeps their cabin.
2. Passengers with the same booking reference travel together on the same flights. Never split a booking group.
3. Seats go to the booking groups by priority, one list for both flights: groups that include a Business passenger first; then larger groups before smaller ones; then by booking reference, alphabetically.
4. Each group gets the connection that arrives in New York earliest and has enough free seats in each of its passengers' cabins on every flight, after all higher-priority groups have their seats. If two such connections arrive at the same time, take the one with fewer changes.
5. If no connection has room for a whole group, leave that group on its cancelled flight.

You may make the bookings in any order.

End your reply with one line in the form `ANSWER: <booking references left on their cancelled flight, comma-separated, or NONE>`.

I'm noting the MUC flight connection times and then sorting the groups by whether they contain business-class tickets, ordering by group size and then alphabetically for ties.

Then I'm working through the seat availability per flight, tracking remaining economy and business seats as I assign each group to its connection option, checking seat counts flight by flight and updating the tallies after each assignment.

D ends up best since 494 E2 and 490 E0 edge out the others, giving a 20:25 departure with one change. For SV5J1N, option B wins over A since option A fails but B gives 472 E1 and 470 E3.

Now I'm ready to actually perform the rebookings: on the ZX 444 connections page, selecting HB3K9W → b, EK1V7P → c, and OR6M2D → a, then choosing passengers Hugo and Mila, clicking radio b, and confirming rebook.
